svg.title: Who Takes a Cut of a Sync Placement
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-sync-catalog-architecture; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: Who Takes a Cut of a Sync Placement; subtitle: Routes from a compounding catalog to the buyer; caption: Michael Elsner models a climb from roughly $2,000 in year one to $75,000-$100,000 by year five as 20 songs a year multiply into stems, instrumentals and edits.; assumptions note: Cut sizes are practitioner estimates and depend on the route chosen; operators split on exclusivity and on pitching supervisors directly.; note: Attributed to Elite Music Coaching (Michael Elsner), Randy McGravey Music, ClintMusic and Majeston.; center: role: Catalog-building composer; headcount: Solo creator writing 20 songs a year; focus: 48 kHz, 24-bit WAVs, clean 8- or 16-bar edit points, sting outros, no samples, deep metadata; spokes: role: Licensing agency; type: Fee-split agent; kpi: Takes 25-50% of the sync fee; role: Music library; type: Catalog holder; kpi: Most keep the fee and publishing; confirm a composer share of sync fees before signing; role: Major sub-publisher; type: Off-the-top distributor; kpi: About 25% off the top; $375 each to library and composer on $1,000; role: Music supervisor; type: Placement buyer; kpi: Searches mood tags; one library track drew 57 placements
